subject: Capacity uplift + invoicing cadence — amendment redline and procurement sync
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@quantixlabs.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity uplift + invoicing cadence — amendment redline and procurement sync

Hi Julia — following our executive sync last week, Quantix confirmed they want to accelerate the reserved capacity: add 150 GPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) across Q1 deployment, and shift billing from monthly pay-as-you-go to quarterly prepay with a 30% prepay discount on committed capacity.

Attached is a first-draft change order (Quantix_CO_v2_redline.docx) that: 
- Adds 150 reserved GPU units under Exhibit B (lines and SKU IDs enumerated)
- Moves invoicing cadence to quarterly with a proposed net-60 payment term on the invoice
- Adds a short implementation milestone schedule and acceptance criteria for the ramp
- Includes a short clause about temporary burst allowance for the first 60 days

Can you confirm: 
1) Procurement acceptance of quarterly prepay + net-60?
2) If Quantix needs a PO number or special invoice fields for payment?
3) Any SOC2/audit evidence they require before signature?

Karthik / Laura / Soojin — can you review the redline and flag any legal/ops items we should preempt (SLA impacts, implementation lead times, price floor language)? I flagged a couple of items in the doc but would rather have legal confirm final language before sending to their procurement team.

Next steps I propose: internal redline clearance by EOD Mon 11/22, then send a clean change order + Docusign link to Quantix procurement. If they need a PO + PO number, we can route to finance for invoice formatting.

Thanks — Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

[Attachment: Quantix_CO_v2_redline.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: Adj_Rate_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, Julia Park <julia@quantixlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + invoicing cadence — amendment redline and procurement sync

Thanks Mateo — quick notes after a skim of the redline: 
- Implementation SLA: We should avoid hard per-hour penalties for the ramp; propose milestone credits instead. Ops has limited calendar availability in Jan due to maintenance windows.
- Billing language: "quarterly prepay" is fine but recommend keeping an option for annual prepay if they want additional discount; also clarify refund/credit behavior on decommissions.
- Payment terms: net-60 on vendor invoice is acceptable but Finance prefers net-45 for new customers by default; if Quantix insists on net-60 we can accept for this deal, but need finance pre-approval.
- Data residency / logging: Soojin, can you confirm whether adding 150 GPUs triggers any additional data handling clause? I think no but want to be sure.

I'll mark the doc with inline comments for the SLA and payment term language. Laura — feel free to add legal guardrails on indemnity and liability caps if this increases committed volume materially.

Karthik

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + invoicing cadence — amendment redline and procurement sync

Hi Mateo / Karthik — thanks, this direction works but a few procurement constraints from our side: 
1) We can accept quarterly prepay. Procurement requires paper to show invoicing cadence and adjusted payment windows; we will issue a PO per quarter (PO numbering convention provided below).
2) We need net-60 terms on the invoice; treasury team will only approve net-60 for C-level contracted deals.
3) We require SOC2 Type II attestation docs and the most recent penetration test summary before the first invoice executes. Can you attach SOC2 + pentest summary, or point to a secure link?
4) For implementation: Quantix cannot accept any SLA financial penalties. Our legal asks that acceptance criteria include a 2-week operational stabilization window after ramp before any performance credits apply.

Procurement contact: Procurement Ops <procure@quantixlabs.com> — they will expect a single change order PDF and a Docusign envelope. PO template: QX-PO-YYYY-#### (we will provide the PO number after Docusign).

If you can send a clean (no markup) PDF and the SOC2 link, we will aim to turn this in 10 business days.

Julia

--
Julia Park
Director of Platform Engineering | Quantix Labs
julia@quantixlabs.com
[Attachment: none]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift + invoicing cadence — amendment redline and procurement sync

Thanks Julia — noted on procurement needs and SOC2. Next steps from Redwood legal/finance/ops: 
1) Legal (me) will accept the stabilization window language but will propose an objective checklist for the 2-week stabilization (basic throughput/latency smoke tests + incident response readiness) rather than open-ended timing. I will add that as Section 3.c in the change order.
2) Finance: Karthik, I'll ping Finance to accept net-60 for QX-2026-0897 and lock the quarterly invoice template; expect confirmation by EOD 11/25.
3) Security: Soojin, please link our SOC2 Type II attestation and the executive summary of our most recent pentest. If you cannot share publicly, provide a secure SharePoint link or the SOC2 upload token.
4) Ops: we'll convert the redline to a clean PDF and prepare a Docusign envelope. Mateo — please confirm the canonical signers for Quantix (we won't proceed until Procurement provides the PO number, but we can prepare the envelope).

I will attach a one-page schedule of acceptance tests and inline the stabilization checklist into the change order. Once we have Procurement's PO number and confirmation on SOC2 access, we'll send Docusign.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel (acting) | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
